title: Janggu (hourglass drum)
summary: The janggu is the hourglass drum of Korean folk and court music. A big, deep head on the left is struck with a padded mallet and a small, bright head on the right with a thin bamboo stick, while red cords and sliding leather rings set the tension. One drummer speaks a low heartbeat and a quick patter together.
howToPlay: The drum lies on its platform: the large head to the left, the small head to the right, the cords at the waist.
Kung is the deep centre of the left head, Dak the bright centre of the right head, and Deok both heads at once at the waist.
Ddak is the crisp tap on the right rim and Kung edge a short tap on the left rim.
A ring closes on the place to strike. Strike as it lands.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The patterns count four beats to the bar, each beat split in three.
heritageNote: Korean drummers learn each rhythm as a spoken line of syllables, Kung, Deok, Dak, before they take up the drum. The syllables sound like the strokes themselves, so a pattern can be chanted, remembered and handed on.
credits: Tradition: the 장구; patterns written for this game
